citations.authors: Gardner RM, Overhage JM, Steen EB, et al.
citations.title: The clinical informatics workforce: an update from the AMIA workforce survey
citations.journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association (JAMIA)
citations.what_it_says: Documents that EHR-vendor-certified analysts (Epic and Cerner) form a core segment of the informatics workforce with strong placement into provider and vendor consulting roles.

citations.title: Health information technology workforce needs: estimating demand under the HITECH Act
citations.what_it_says: Projected sustained demand for EHR-vendor-trained analysts (including Cerner) and supported the federal investment in workforce pipelines that now favor multi-vendor literacy.

citations.title: Occupational Outlook Handbook: Medical and Health Services Managers / Computer Occupations
citations.what_it_says: Reports health informatics and EHR analyst roles among the fastest-growing healthcare-adjacent occupations, with median wages well above bedside clinical medians.

citations.authors: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs / Oracle Health
citations.title: Federal Electronic Health Record Modernization Program Update
citations.what_it_says: VA and DoD continued rollout of Oracle Cerner Millennium sustains federal demand for certified Cerner/Oracle Health analysts and consultants.

citations.title: HIMSS Health Informatics Workforce Survey
citations.what_it_says: Survey finds Cerner-certified analysts represent roughly 20-25% of EHR-credentialed respondents, with median compensation trailing Epic-certified peers by a modest margin.

citations.title: Transitioning from clinical practice to clinical informatics: a qualitative study
citations.what_it_says: Clinician-to-informaticist transitions are most successful when paired with employer-sponsored vendor certification (Epic or Cerner) obtained during an initial analyst hire.

citations.authors: Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology (ONC)
citations.title: Hospital EHR Vendors — Health IT Dashboard: Market Share of Certified Health IT Vendors Reported by Hospitals Participating in the CMS EHR Incentive Programs
citations.journal: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, ONC
citations.what_it_says: ONC's Health IT Dashboard reports Oracle Cerner as the second-largest certified EHR vendor among U.S. non-federal acute-care hospitals, trailing Epic, with the two vendors together accounting for the majority of acute-care hospital EHR market share.
